Rashi on Nedarim 9b:10:1.hebrew: א"ה אפי' נזיר טהור - דדלמא מתחרט על נזירותו, ונמצא מביא חולין לעזרה:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:10:1.english: If so, even a pure nazirite - For perhaps he regrets his naziriteship, and [thus] ends up bringing unconsecrated [animals] into the Temple Courtyard.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:10:2.hebrew: בנזיר טהור - ליכא למיחש דמתחרט, דכיון דלא נטמא ולא רבו עליו ימי טומאה, ודאי לא מתחרט. ואי אמרת אפ"ה הוא מתחרט דאינו יכול לעמוד בנזירותו, להא ליכא למיחש, דאי לאו דאמיד בנפשיה קודם שנדר דיכול לעמוד בו, לא הוה נדר, ולא מיתחרט כל היכא דלא נטמא:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:10:2.english: In [the case of] a ritually pure nazirite - There is no [reason] to be concerned that he regrets [his vow], for since he did not become ritually impure and days of impurity did not increase upon him, he certainly does not regret [it]. And if you say [that] even so he regrets [it] because he is unable to uphold his naziriteship, there is no [reason] to be concerned about this, for had he not assessed himself before he vowed that he is able to uphold it, he would not have vowed; and he does not regret [it] in any case where he did not become ritually impure.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:1:1.hebrew: כי קאמר ר"מ בנדר - אסור בלשון נדרים דוקא קאמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:1:1.english: When Rabbi Meir said [it], [he was referring] to a vow - He specifically meant [that it is] forbidden [when expressed] in the language of vows.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:1:2.hebrew: אבל בנדבה לא אמר - והיינו מתני' דקתני כנדבתם, דכשרין נדרי בלשון נדבה:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:1:2.english: But regarding a gift [offering] he did not say [it] - And this is [what] the Mishnah [means] when it teaches "like their gift offerings," for the virtuous vow using the language of a gift offering.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:1:3.english: But it is taught: "Like their gift offerings" — he has vowed, etc. - For it implies that he says [it] in the language of a vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:2:1.hebrew: דלמא אתי בה לידי תקלה - דכי אמר בל' נדר הרי עלי קרבן, אתי בה לידי תקלה, דעבר משום בל תאחר:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:2:1.english: Perhaps he will come through it to a stumbling block - For when he says in the language of a vow, "Behold, [it is incumbent] upon me [to bring] an offering," he comes through it to a stumbling block, as he transgresses [the prohibition of] "Do not delay."

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:2:2.hebrew: נדבה נמי - כי אמר הרי זו קרבן, אתי בהו לידי תקלה, לידי גיזה ועבודה. א] אבל בבל תאחר לא, דכל היכא דאיתא, בי גזא דרחמנא איתא:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:2:2.english: A gift [offering] also - When one says, "Behold, this is an offering," he may come through it to a stumbling block — [namely,] to shearing and working [with the animal]. However, [with respect to the prohibition of] "do not delay," [that is] not [the concern here], for wherever it is, it is [already] in the treasury of the Merciful One.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:3:1.hebrew: [כהלל] - מתני' דקתני נדבה מותר, כגון דעביד כהלל דמקדישה בעזרה, דחו לא אתי בה לידי מטילה:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:3:1.english: [Like Hillel] - [Regarding] the Mishnah that teaches [that] a gift-offering is permitted: [it is] for example where he acts like Hillel, who consecrates it in the Temple courtyard, so that he does not thereby come to [commit] misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:4:1.hebrew: נדבה דנזירות מאי איכא למימר - היכי עביד דלא ליתי לידי תקלה, דקתני נדב בנזיר דמותר, דכשרים מתנדבים בנזירות:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:4:1.english: [With regard to] a voluntary vow of naziriteship, what is there to say - How does he act so that he does not come to a stumbling block, since it teaches [concerning one who] vowed as a nazirite that it is permitted, as the righteous make voluntary vows of naziriteship?

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:4:2.english: He holds in accordance with Shimon HaTzaddik - That [one] takes a nazirite vow for the sake of Heaven, like that [person] who came before Shimon HaTzaddik.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:5:1.hebrew: לא אכלתי אשם נזיר טמא - דנזיר שמיטמא מביא אשם, ואח"כ מונה ימי נזירות אחר. ומאותו אשם לא אכל, וטעמא מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:5:1.english: I did not eat the guilt-offering of a ritually impure nazirite - For a nazirite who becomes ritually impure brings a guilt-offering, and afterward counts days of another naziriteship. And from that guilt-offering he did not eat, and [the Gemara] explains the reason below.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:5:2.english: A certain man came before me - [Meaning] that he came to offer the sacrifice of his naziriteship and to shave his hair.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:6:1.hebrew: ופחז יצרי עלי - מתוך שראיתי במים צורתי כל כך נאה, נתגבר עלי יצרי ובקש להביאני לידי מעשים רעים, לטורדני מן העולם:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:6:1.english: And my inclination surged upon me - Because I saw my form in the water [was] so handsome, my [evil] inclination overpowered me and sought to bring me to evil deeds, to expel me from the world.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:7:1.english: I said to him - Thus he himself said.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:7:2.hebrew: עליך הכתוב אומר איש כי יפליא כו' - דהיינו לה', לשם שמים:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:7:2.english: About you the verse states: "When a man shall clearly utter [a vow]," etc. - That is, "to the Lord" — for the sake of Heaven.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:8:1.hebrew: דאתי על חטא - שטימא עצמו. וכיון דאתי על חטא הוא, א"כ לא בעי למיכל שום קרבן חטאת. אלא היינו טעמא דלא אכל אשם נזיר טמא:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:8:1.english: That it comes for a sin - [In] that he made himself ritually impure. And since it is because it comes for a sin, if so, he would not want to eat any sin-offering. Rather, this is the reason he did not eat the guilt-offering of a ritually impure nazirite:

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:9:1.hebrew: כשהן תוהין - מתפחדים, כמו ופחדת לילה ויומם (דברים כ״ח:ס״ו), ומתרגמינן ותהית. כשהן כועסין נודרין, שאינן נודרים לשם שמים, אלא לשם כעס מנזרין עצמי:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:9:1.english: When they are afraid - [This means] they are frightened, as [in the verse,] "and you shall fear night and day" (Deuteronomy 28:66), which we translate [in Aramaic] as "uteheit." When they are angry, they take vows, for they do not vow for the sake of Heaven; rather, out of anger they make themselves nazirites.

Rashi on Nedarim 9b:9:2.hebrew: וכשהן מטמאין - דאתא טומאה וסתרי להנהו יומי דנזירות, ובעו למימני יומי נזירות אחר, וריבה עליהן ימי טומאה — דשמא מיטמא פעם אחרת ובעי למיסתר כל הני יומי דנזירות — ומתחרטין בעצמן שנדרו. וכיון דמתחרטין, לא הוי נזירות לש"ש, ונמצאו מביאין חולין לעזרה. ומשו"ה לא אכל אלא מזה, דודאי לש"ש הוא דעבד:
Rashi on Nedarim 9b:9:2.english: And when they become ritually impure - For ritual impurity comes and voids those days of naziriteship, and they must count other days of naziriteship, and the days of impurity increase upon them — for perhaps one will become impure another time and will have to void all these days of naziriteship — and they regret within themselves that they vowed. And since they regret [it], [the] naziriteship is not for the sake of Heaven, and they turn out to be bringing non-sacred [animals] into the [Temple] courtyard. Therefore, he did not eat except from this one, for he certainly acted for the sake of Heaven.

Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:1:1.hebrew: והא קתני כנדבתם - תימה: מגופיה דמתני' תיקשי ליה, דקתני "כנדבתם" והדר קתני "נדר"! וי"ל דאין ה"נ, ולשנויא ניחא הכל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:1:1.english: But it teaches "like their gift offerings" - [This is] puzzling: let [the Gemara] raise the difficulty from the Mishnah itself, for it teaches "like their gift offerings" and then teaches "he has vowed"! And one can say that indeed it is so, and according to the [Gemara's] answer, everything is resolved.

Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:3:1.hebrew: כהלל הזקן שמביאין בעזרה - וא"ת: אכתי היכי קרי ליה "נדבת כשרים", הא ליכא שריותא כ"א כהלל כשהבהמה בעזרה, ומתני' משמע בכל ענין? ועוד, דהא תינח נדרי קרבן, אבל נדרי דקונם — כגון שאוסר ככר עליו — התם לא שייך טעם זה! ואומר הר"ר אליעזר: כיון דכשרים מתנדבים בשום צד בעזרה, גם חוץ לעזרה נמי תפיס שפיר הנדבה בלשון זה, ואף על גב דכשרים לא מתנדבים כה"ג. אבל "נדרי כשרים" לא הוו כלל בשום צד: אף כשהיא בעזרה נמי איכא חששא שמא תמות ויהא חייב באחריות, ואתי לידי תקלה ד"בל תאחר"; הלכך, "כנדרי כשרים" לא אמר כלום:
Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:3:1.english: "Like Hillel the Elder," [meaning] that they bring [the animal] into the Temple courtyard - And if you ask: Still, how can [the Mishnah] call it "the gift-offering of the righteous," [when] there is no permissibility except [to act] like Hillel when the animal is in the Temple courtyard, whereas the Mishnah implies [it takes effect] in any manner? And furthermore, this works well for vows of an offering, but [as for] vows of konam — such as when one prohibits a loaf [of bread] upon himself — there this reason does not apply! And Rabbi Eliezer says: Since the righteous do make gift-offerings in some way — [namely,] in the Temple courtyard — even outside the Temple courtyard as well, the gift-offering takes effect properly with this wording, even though the righteous do not make gift-offerings in such a manner. However, "the vows of the righteous" do not exist at all in any way: even when [the animal] is in the Temple courtyard, there is still the concern lest it die and he be liable for its replacement, and he would come to the stumbling block of [violating] "do not delay" (bal te'acher); therefore, [one who says] "like the vows of the righteous" has said nothing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:4:1.hebrew: דנזירות מאי איכא למימר - והלא מיד שנדר קם ליה בבל יאכל ובבל ישתה, ואיכא חששא לתקלה שמא יעבור. ומשני: כי ההיא דשמעון הצדיק, דנדר נזירות לשם שמים מאהבה, ולכך קרי ליה נדבה, כדכתיב (שמות לה): "כל נדיב לב". וא"ת: והלא כל הכשרים שמתנדבים לשם שמים נודרין בלשון נדר, [וא"כ] "כנדרי כשרים" אמאי לא אמר כלום? אף כי שמא זה אינו מתכוין לשם שמים, תופס שפיר הלשון, כיון שיש כשרים שנודרים נזירות לשם שמים, מידי דהוה אנדבת כשרים דקרבן לפירוש הר"ר אליעזר וכדפרישית לעיל! וי"ל: דמ"מ "נדר כשר" לא מיקרי כלל, דנדר משמע מה שאדם נודר מדאגת יסורים מעונותיהם ולא מאהבת המקום; אבל כשרים תופס שפיר, דנדבה משמע מאהבה, דכתיב (הושע יד): "אהבם נדבה", אלמא נדבה משמע מאהבה. וכן בתוספ' קתני: "כנדבת רשעים" לא אמר כלום, לפי שאין הרשעים מתנדבין כלל; ואע"ג דכמה מתנדבים בלשון נדבה ואומרים "הרי זו עולה", מ"מ לא מיקרי נדבה, משום שאין עושין מנדבת לבם מאהבה רק מדאגת יסורים מעונותיהם. "כנדבת רשעים" אינו קרויין נדבה, לפי שאין עושין מאהבת המקום; "נדרי כשרים" נמי אינו קרוי נדר, כיון שאין עושין מדאגת יסורים אלא מאהבה, (אלא) קרוי נדבה. ולכך קרי נזירות כשרין "נדבתם", אע"ג דבלשון נדר נמי, דכל נזירות בלשון נדר הוא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:4:1.english: [Regarding] naziriteship, what is there to say? - Isn't it so that as soon as he vowed [to become a nazirite], he is bound by [the prohibitions of] "he shall not eat" and "he shall not drink," and there is concern for a stumbling block, lest he transgress? And [the Gemara] answers: Like that [case] of Shimon HaTzaddik, where he vowed naziriteship for the sake of Heaven out of love; and therefore [the Mishnah] calls it a "freewill gift," as it is written (Exodus 35): "everyone whose heart was willing." And if you should ask: Do not all the righteous who donate for the sake of Heaven vow using the language of a vow (neder)? [And if so,] why has he said nothing [when he says] "like the vows of the righteous"? Even though perhaps this [speaker] does not intend [it] for the sake of Heaven, the language should take effect properly, since there are righteous people who vow naziriteship for the sake of Heaven — just as is the case with "the freewill gift of the righteous" regarding an offering, according to the explanation of R. Eliezer, and as I explained above! One may answer: Nevertheless, it is not called "a vow of a righteous person" at all, for a vow (neder) implies what a person vows out of fear of afflictions on account of their sins, and not out of love of the Omnipresent; whereas [the freewill gift of] the righteous takes effect properly, for a freewill gift (nedavah) implies out of love, as it is written (Hosea 14): "I will love them freely (nedavah)," thus [proving that] a freewill gift implies out of love. And similarly, in the Tosefta it is taught: [If one says] "like the freewill gift of the wicked," he has said nothing, because the wicked do not offer freewill gifts at all; and even though many [wicked people] donate using the language of a freewill gift and say, "This [animal] is a burnt-offering," nevertheless it is not called a freewill gift, because they do not do [it] from the willingness of their heart out of love, only out of fear of afflictions on account of their sins. "Like the freewill gift of the wicked" — they are not called a freewill gift, because they do not act out of love of the Omnipresent; "the vows of the righteous" also is not called a vow, since they do not act out of fear of afflictions, rather out of love, (rather) it is called a freewill gift. And therefore [the Mishnah] calls the naziriteship of the righteous "their freewill gift," even though [it is] also in the language of a vow, for all naziriteship is in the language of a vow.

Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:9:1.hebrew: כשהן תוהין נודרין - תוהין — לשון "ותוהא על הראשונות"; כלומר, כשהן תוהין בעונותיהם ודואגין מן היסורין, נודרין להגין מן היסורין, וכשרבים עליהם ימי טומאה, מתחרטין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 9b:9:1.english: When they regret, they vow - Tohin [is] an expression [as in] "and he regrets the earlier [deeds]"; that is to say, when they regret their sins and worry because of suffering, they vow [to become nazirites] in order to protect [themselves] from suffering, and when the days of ritual impurity increase upon them, they regret [it].
